headline: Roman had a fall on 10/19, new evening confusion since late October (stove left on once), 8.6% weight loss over about 12 weeks, and a decline in bathing and dressing independence. Several follow-ups are not documented.

items.statement: On 11/09 his niece Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. Roman was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The plan was urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week. The notes provided show no results or visit for these.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 11/09 nursing note. The statement that no results or visit appear in the provided notes is a fair caveat.

items.statement: Roman fell at home in the kitchen on 10/19 while reaching for a cabinet. Niece Linda found him on the floor. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness, had a small left forearm skin tear, and fall risk was reassessed as high. On 10/24 PT found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see him twice weekly.
items.verifier_note: The 10/19 nursing note and 10/24 PT evaluation support every detail, including the fall circumstances, the injury, high fall risk, gait, TUG, recommendations and twice-weekly PT.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg on 9/5 to 79.8 (10/1), 77.3 (10/28) and 75.2 kg on 11/24. That is -7.1 kg (-8.6%). On 11/24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfasts and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. Plan: oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check for chewing problems.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record gives all four weights and the -7.1 kg (-8.6%) change. The dietitian note supports poor appetite, skipped breakfast, about 50% of lunches eaten, and the plan. The note rounds the loss to 9%, which is consistent.

items.statement: On 9/18 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting out of the tub, and Roman said he has been skipping showers for fear of slipping. On 9/25 OT found he now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing (independent at last review). OT recommended a tub transfer bench, handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing. The notes do not show whether these were put in place.
items.verifier_note: Both notes support the aide's report, the OT findings (including independence at last review) and the recommendations. The statement that implementation is not shown is accurate, since the notes are silent on it.

items.statement: A PT note dated 10/24 says the 10/19 fall is resolved, he is at baseline, and it was removed from the problem list. This conflicts with the PT evaluation the same day, which found unsteady gait, Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds and twice-weekly PT. It also conflicts with the high fall risk documented on 10/19.
items.verifier_note: The n016 note says the fall is resolved, he is at baseline, and it was removed from the problem list. It conflicts with the same-day PT evaluation (unsteady gait, TUG 19 s, twice-weekly PT) and with the high fall risk documented on 10/19.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 11/09 completed, and what were the results?
Is it safe for Roman to be alone at home with the stove given the evening confusion? Is a safety plan needed?
Which equipment and services are in place: walker, grab bars, tub transfer bench, handheld shower, home safety evaluation and added bathing hours?
Should the fall be kept on the active problem list, given the conflicting 10/24 PT notes?
Could the weight loss, confusion, falls and functional decline be related, and who will review them together?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the last IDT review/enrollment context (enrolled 2024-10-07) is reflected in the chart before comparing changes.

Falls and injuries: count falls, near-falls, and fall-related injuries in the window; note any fall-risk factors given osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, fibromyalgia, and the use of metoprolol and nitroglycerin (orthostasis risk).

ED visits and hospital admissions: list dates, reasons, discharge summaries, and any follow-up appointments completed or missed, with focus on chest pain, ischemic heart disease, COPD/bronchitis exacerbations, and blood pressure problems.

Medication reconciliation: compare active list (metoprolol succinate 100 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, naproxen sodium 220 mg, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin 20 mg) against changes in the window; flag any new starts, stops, dose changes, or refills that lapsed.

Bleeding-risk review: naproxen combined with clopidogrel in a patient with anemia and ischemic heart disease. Check for GI bleeding signs, new bruising, melena, hemoglobin/hematocrit trends, and whether the team has documented a discussion of the NSAID use.
Pain management: track pain scores, frequency of pain-related contacts, use of non-drug therapies, and any changes to analgesics given chronic pain, fibromyalgia, and knee osteoarthritis.

Cardiac and blood pressure trend: review BP readings (including orthostatic readings if taken), heart rate on beta-blocker, chest pain episodes and nitroglycerin use frequency, and any cardiology or primary care visits.
Respiratory status: review oxygen saturation, inhaler use or respiratory symptoms, and any COPD-related visits, given chronic obstructive bronchitis history.

Metabolic and weight trend: record weight and BMI trend (obesity, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes), most recent glucose or HbA1c, lipid results on simvastatin, and nutrition or activity counseling completed.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: check ADL/IADL changes, mobility aids, mood screening and attendance at PACE center or day program, any cognitive screen changes, and caregiver or social-support changes; list care-plan items due or overdue (assessments, reassessments, goals) by the review date 2026-11-30. Note that allergies are recorded as empty and should be confirmed.
